messages:
sam: Heads-up — scorecard diffs look off after landing quantize-v2. The 'delta' chart shows large negative improvements for almost every model, even baselines.

jordana: Which view? compare table or the per-model card?

kevin: Compare table (the multi-run diff). I grabbed a quick export and it looks like baselines were remapped. All rows point to the same baseline alias.

mira: I dug into the runner export: we recently added `baseline_model_alias` to the CSV, but the dashboard query still expects `baseline_model_id`. When alias exists we end up joining on the wrong column and it falls back to the first model in the group.

eval-runner-bot: CI: eval-runner/export-schema check failed on job #2312 — schema_version mismatch (expected v3, got v4). See logs: https://ci.internal/eval/2312

sam: That would definitely cause the symptom. Can we either backfill alias->id mapping or make the dashboard accept alias?

kevin: Short term: dashboard patch that prefers `baseline_model_id` then `baseline_model_alias`. Longer term: pin schema and add tests.

jordana: I'll open a tiny fix for the dashboard mapping. Also adding a unit test to the scorecard service that simulates the CSV export with alias only.

mira: I think there's a second issue: my local run shows duplicate sample IDs in the export for quantized sharded runs — looks like the shard-merge step didn't dedupe properly. That would make drilldowns show duplicated examples.

kevin: Ugh. So two things: wrong baseline join + duplicated samples. We should triage order: fix dashboard join so UI isn't broken, then fix runner merge.

jordana: Agreed. Pushing mapping patch now. Patch adds SQL fallback and a defensive GROUP BY on sample_id for drilldown joins.

kevin: Example SQL snippet that should be applied in dashboard service: 
```
SELECT r.run_id, COALESCE(r.baseline_model_id, m.id) AS baseline_id, d.sample_id, d.metric_delta
FROM run_exports r
JOIN models m ON m.alias = r.baseline_model_alias OR m.id = r.baseline_model_id
LEFT JOIN drilldown d ON d.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id, baseline_id, d.sample_id
```

jordana: landed PR: #482. Added integration test and a guard that fails fast if `schema_version` missing. Deploying to staging.

deploy-bot: deploy started — stack:scorecard-service staging, commit: 7f9c3b4 (#482) :rocket:

jordana: Deployed to staging. Per-run compare looks fixed, diff charts render correctly now. Still seeing duplicate samples in one quantize-v2 run though (mira?).

mira: Yep, the duplicate issue reproducible locally. I traced it to `shard_merge()` logic — we append instead of dedup when `sort_key` absent for streaming exports. Will push a patch to ensure deterministic keys and use a set.

kevin: Please add a small CI test that runs a sharded export with overlapping sample ids to catch regressions.

mira: Will do. Adding test + fix in runner PR #211. Also bumping export schema to v4 intentionally and updating eval-runner CI step to validate version.

sam: Nice. Once both PRs pass canary to prod. Also schedule a short postmortem note in the incidents backlog so we have a written record.

jordana: Can someone add an alert rule? Proposal: alert if >5% of compare queries in 1h return a >50% identical-baseline rate. That catches remapping regressions.

kevin: Added alert draft in pagerduty -> scorecard team: `scorecard.baseline_remap_rate > 0.05` with runbook link.

deploy-bot: staging health check passed for stack:scorecard-service commit: 7f9c3b4

jordana: Running integration smoke now. If green, will request prod deploy tonight at 11pm PT.

sam: Sounds good. Thanks all. Please tag me in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
